new_statements.quote: Stress: Stress as a distinctive phonetic feature occurs on vowels. There are three predictable variations in stress with which vowels occur (a) acute marked ['] over the vowel. (b) normal or medium stress unmarked [ ] and (c) lax or stress-less marked [ - ] over the vowel. [p. 26:] (1) The acute stress [ ' ] occurs on a vowel when the vowel is followed by an aspirated consonant or a glottal fricative and is not preceded by an aspirated consonant or a glottal fricative. ... (2) The lax variety [ - ] occurs on a long vowel when the vowel is preceded by an aspirated consonant or a glottal fricative and is not followed by either an aspirated consonant or a glottal fricative. ... (3) The normal or medium stress which is unmarked occurs on vowels elsewhere. ... All these three varieties are complementarily distributed and are treated as allophones of one stress phoneme.
new_statements.citation: Ranganatha, M. R. 1981 [foreword 1 Sept 1980]. Survey of Mandeali and Kului in Himachal Pradesh. Census of India 1971, Language Monograph No. 7. New Delhi: Office of the Registrar General, India, Language Division.
new_statements.locator: Part II Mandeali, I. Phonemics, 'Stress', printed pp. 25-26 (PDF pp. 35-36)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened via its extracted text layer (180 form-feed pages) and the two page renders / -printed pp. 25-26 = PDF pp. 35-36). The quoted passage is there verbatim: p. 25 bottom 'Stress: Stress as a distinctive phonetic feature occurs on vowels. There are three predictable variations in stress with which vowels occur (a) acute marked ['] over the vowel. (b) normal or medium stress unmarked [ ] and (c) lax or stress-less marked [ - ] over the vowel.'; p. 26 '(1) The acute stress [ ' ] occurs on a vowel when the vowel is followed by an aspirated consonant or a glottal fricative and is not preceded by an aspirated consonant or a glottal fricative... (2) The lax variety [ - ] occurs on a long vowel…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only accessible first-hand description treats 'stress' not as a positional word-level prominence but as three predictable degrees of vowel prominence conditioned by adjacent aspirates: a vowel is 'acute' (high/strong) when followed but not preceded by an aspirated consonant or /h/, 'lax' (weak, extra-long) when preceded but not followed by one, and 'medium' elsewhere. No rule locating stress by syllable position or weight is given; the author adds that 'this analysis of stress is only tentative' and that stress, vowel length and aspiration interact in the syllable patterns. The pattern described is the aspiration-conditioned pitch/prominence typical of Punjabi-type tonogenesis in Western Pahari rather than a word-stress rule.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the author qualifies the whole analysis as tentative for lack of time and data, and notes that recognising phonemic stress avoids positing three contrastive vowel lengths (p. 26).
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for vowels within the word ('a sequence of phonemes between two pauses'); elicited citation forms (c. 1100 words, 500 sentences, stories) from two matriculate informants of Purani Mandi, Mandi town, fieldwork June-July 1965 and 1966. Later census sketch (LSI Himachal Pradesh, Mukherjee) lists only length and nasalization as suprasegmentals and is silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Ranganatha 1981 describes 'Standard Mandeali' as spoken by educated speakers of Purani Mandi, Mandi town (two informants, fieldwork 1965-66); this is the standard dialect of mand1409, not the North Mandeali / Chhota Banghali / Mandeali Pahari / Suketi varieties distinguished by Bailey 1908 and Grierson 1916.

sources.citation: Ranganatha, M. R. 1981 [foreword dated 1 Sept 1980]. Survey of Mandeali and Kului in Himachal Pradesh (Census of India 1971, Language Monograph No. 7). New Delhi: Office of the Registrar General, India, Language Division. x+168 pp. Mandeali phonemics pp. 17-29.
sources.note: Pp. 25-26 'Stress': stress 'occurs on vowels' in three predictable, complementarily distributed varieties - acute on a vowel followed (not preceded) by an aspirated consonant or /h/, lax on a long vowel preceded (not followed) by an aspirate or /h/, medium elsewhere; treated as allophones of one stress phoneme, left unmarked; author calls the analysis 'only tentative'. No positional (syllable-counting or weight) rule for word stress is given.

sources.note: Silent: section 2.1.2 'Suprasegmental Phonemes' (p. 452) lists only vowel Length and Nasalization; no mention of stress, accent or tone anywhere in the Mandeali chapter.

sources.note: Silent: the Mandeali introduction (pp. 717-720) discusses pronunciation of vowels and consonants relative to Kangri but says nothing about accent or stress; grep of accent/stress/tone/pitch over pp. 717-769 finds only a gloss word.

sources.citation: Bailey, T. Grahame. 1908. The Languages of the Northern Himalayas, being studies in the grammar of twenty-six Himalayan dialects. London: Royal Asiatic Society. Part II 'Dialects of Mandi State': Grammar of Mandeali; Notes on North Mandeali.
sources.note: Silent for Mandeali: the Mandeali grammar is morphology plus a transliteration note; the book's remarks on accent (e.g. antepenult accent of -ada participles, h raising the tone of its syllable) are in the Chamba-dialect part, not the Mandi part.
